predecessors.name: Ottoman Empire
predecessors.text: the Tihamah coastal strip, about 80 mi long and 40 mi inland around Sabya and Jizan, where Muhammad ibn Ali al-Idrisi 'began to establish political control' about 1906; the Ottomans had held Asir…

successors.name: Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd
successors.text: Abha and the highlands (taken 1920) and, by 1923, 'the rest of Asir' in the Tihamah; the Saudis' Emirate of Nejd row

successors.name: Emirate of Nejd
successors.text: Abha and the highlands, taken in 1920 and divided with al-Idrisi's Tihamah tribes in the fall of 1920

successors.name: North Yemen
successors.text: Hodeidah (and Al Luhayyah): the Hodeidah page has 'Yemen captured the city in April 1925'; the Mutawakkilite page has Imam Yahya capturing it after Muhammad ibn Ali al-Idrisi's death ('after 1923')

ledger.x: 1907: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Idrisi's emirate begins on the Tihamah coast.
1909: the Idrisi take Az Zaydiyah and Al Luhayyah.
1911: the Idrisi lose the two towns.
1919: Britain hands Al Luhayyah to Asir.
1919: war with Imam Yahya begins over the Tihamah to Hodeidah.
1920: the Saudis take Abha and the highlands.
29 January 1921: Hodeidah passes to the Emirate.
1925: Al Luhayyah passes to Yemen with Hodeidah.

April 1925: the war with Imam Yahya over Hodeidah ends with his capture of the town ('Yemen captured the city in April 1925', Hodeidah page), after the Emirate page's span of intermittent warfare in 1919-1923.
1926: the Emir of Asir accepts Saudi suzerainty.
20 November 1930: the suzerainty ends in incorporation.
20 November 1930: the Idrisid emirate is absorbed by the Saudis.

wars.name: Idrisi-Ottoman fighting for Asir
wars.outcome: The Idrisi took Az Zaydiyah and Al Luhayyah in autumn 1909, made peace at al-Hafa'ir (ratified January 1910, al-Idrisi becoming Kaymakam of Asir) and fought again from October 1910; in 1915 al-Idrisi allied with Britain and took the Farasan Islands.

wars.name: Idrisi-Yemeni conflict over Hodeidah
wars.outcome: Intermittent warfare with Imam Yahya, who considered Hodeidah part of Yemen; the Idrisids received Hodeidah on 29 January 1921 when Britain evacuated it, and Yemen captured it in April 1925 (Hodeidah page; the Mutawakkilite page: after the death of Muhammad…

wars.name: Saudi conquest of Asir
wars.outcome: The Saudis took Abha in 1920, divided the tribes with al-Idrisi in the fall of 1920 and 'incorporated the rest of Asir by 1923' (the highlands; the Tihamah emirate lasted to 1930).

certainty.note: Tribal and coastal frontiers; no page opened gives a treaty line (the fall-1920 Saudi-Idrisi treaty divides tribes, not a boundary).
